findings.title: Accidental git submodule `sentry-repo` committed at repository root
findings.body: The PR adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink/submodule entry (`Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a`) without a corresponding `.gitmodules` entry. This will cause `git submodule` commands and checkouts with `--recurse-submodules` to fail. Remove the `sentry-repo` entry from the commit.

findings.title: Upsampling cache key uses non-deterministic `hash()` and caches across test cases
findings.body: In `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` (line 27) and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` (line 73), the shared cache key is constructed with Python's built-in `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. Because `PYTHONHASHSEED` is randomized per process by default, different worker processes will compute different cache keys for the same `(organization_id, project_ids)`, so `invalidate_upsampling_cache` called in one worker will fail to invalidate entries written by other workers, and different project ID tuples can collide under a 64-bit hash. In addition, caching this in `sentry.utils.cache` (when `sentry.options` already caches option values in memory/Redis) causes stale cache hits in tests when `options.get` is mocked across requests for the same projects. Either rely on `sentry.options`'s built-in caching directly, or use a deterministic representation (e.g. a comma-joined sorted list or SHA-256 digest) for the cache key.

findings.title: `_get_event_stats` passes outer `dataset` instead of `scoped_dataset` to upsampling check
findings.body: Inside `_get_event_stats`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` is called with the outer `dataset` variable rather than the `scoped_dataset` parameter or `query` argument. When `get_event_stats_factory` splits a dashboard widget query (lines 362-452), it invokes `_get_event_stats` with `scoped_dataset=discover` and a modified `query` (such as `f"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction"` or `f"({query}) AND event.type:transaction"`), while the outer `dataset` is `metrics_enhanced_performance` or `metrics_performance`. Because `dataset` is not `errors` or `discover`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` always returns `False` for those split queries even when querying error events on `discover`. Pass `scoped_dataset` (and check the effective `query` string) instead of the outer `dataset`.

findings.title: `upsampled_count` sums `sample_weight` without handling NULL/0 values for unsampled events
findings.body: `upsampled_count` is defined as `Function("toInt64", [Function("sum", [Column("sample_weight")])], alias)`. In Snuba's errors/discover schema, events ingested without client error sampling (or historical events ingested before `sample_weight` was populated) have `sample_weight` as `NULL` or `0` rather than `1.0`. Summing `sample_weight` directly means unsampled events contribute `0` to the count instead of `1` (e.g., a bucket containing only unsampled events will report a count of `0`). Use `ifNull(if(greater(sample_weight, 0), sample_weight, 1), 1)` (or `greatest(sample_weight, 1)`) inside the sum so each unsampled event still counts as 1.

findings.title: Unrelated change to `topEvents <= 0` error message breaks existing endpoint contract/tests
findings.body: Line 124 changes the 400 error message for `topEvents <= 0` from `"If topEvents needs to be at least 1"` to `"topEvents needs to be at least 1"`. This is unrelated to error upsampling and changes the response payload asserted by existing `OrganizationEventsStatsEndpoint` tests.
